The shape of this HN duplicate detector actually works as a GitHub uptime chart:

https://news.ycombinator.com/from?site=githubstatus.com

It's driven by aggregated user complaints, so it's pretty high-quality. Comment counts are a proxy for "how bad was the outage" + "how long was the outage thread topical for".

edit to add: Here's a scatterplot of the same,

https://files.catbox.moe/hhfh4l.png

I think all they have to do is stop giving free CI to everyone and this reliability issue will be solved immediately.

Disclaimer: I am building a code forge myself at https://juju.bi
It bugs me how there can be an acknowledged live incident happening today with Actions, and yet down the page where it shows last 30d uptime for actions, today's little rectangle is a chipper green.
Lesson for every infra provider: physically separate your free tier infra from your paid tier infra.

Self-hosted GitHub Actions on AWS spot are still working.

After many outages we had to build our own free runner https://github.com/supercorp-ai/superci

Ever since I switched to Forgejo (could do Gitea or other self-hosted too), my outages have gone down to basically zero. It’s only down when I do maintenance but since I’m not pushing code at the same time it doesn’t matter
